1. Executive Summary & Research Mission

Natural products from biological matrices represent the primary scaffold source for modern drug discovery. However, untargeted metabolomics via Collision-Induced Dissociation (CID) tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) remains a formidable challenge: complex stochastic bond breakages, instrument-dependent collision energies, and dynamic ionization efficiencies hinder direct reverse-engineering of molecular structures.

This project formulates an end-to-end, high-throughput computational pipeline engineered specifically for the Enveda CASMI 2026 competition. We train a multi-scale deep neural network (SpectrumFPNet, 28.78M parameters) over 2,539,608 experimental tandem mass spectra across 60 rigorous epochs (1,130,940 gradient descent updates over 52.7 GPU hours). The network directly maps 12,001-dimensional binned and normalized spectra into 2048-bit Morgan chemical fingerprint vectors (ECFP4), capturing planar molecular topologies and heteroatom environments.

2. Complete Dataset Architecture & Big-Data Chunking

A central architectural innovation was managing the sheer computational mass of the dataset without overflowing host system memory:

Dataset Partition Number of Spectra Batches (B=128) Storage / Footprint Scientific Role & Function
Raw Master Cohort 2,539,608 19,842 3.03 GB (Parquet) Full experimental corpus containing diverse collision energies and ionization modes.
Training Split (95%) 2,412,628 18,849 118.44 GB (1,270 Chunks) Dense float32 binned arrays streamed via PyTorch IterableDataset across 60 epochs.
Validation Split (5%) 126,980 993 ~6.2 GB (NPZ) Strictly held-out during backpropagation; monitored every epoch for loss and AP minimum.
Test Query Cohort 1,213 1 Chunk (test_00001) 55.5 MB (NPZ) / 4.6 MB Parquet 400 unique natural product molecules measured across multiple collision energies.
Candidate Database 275,810 N/A 25.8 MB (FP) + 1.1 MB (Mass) Curated unique chemical structures searched via continuous Tanimoto similarity.
Key Technical Explanations for Academic Defense:
• Why is the Training Set 118.44 GB? 2,539,608 spectra × 12,000 bins × 4 bytes (float32) ≈ 121.9 GB. Storing this in RAM causes out-of-memory kernel termination. Splitting it into 1,270 chunk files of 2,000 spectra each allowed streaming multi-worker training.
• Why does Test contain only one file (test_00001.npz)? The competition test cohort consists of 1,213 spectra total. Because 1,213 < 2,000 (chunk size), the entire test cohort fits into a single contiguous chunk. These 1,213 spectra correspond to 400 distinct molecules, each tested at ~3 collision energies (e.g., 10 eV, 20 eV, 40 eV) and pooled via median aggregation.

4. Neural Architecture & Systematic Hyperparameter Tuning

The neural architecture, designated SpectrumFPNet, was designed to solve the structural inversion problem: converting continuous fragment intensity distributions into discrete molecular graphs.

Network Tensor Pipeline:
Input Vector x in R^12,001 ⟶ Linear(12,001 → 2048) → BatchNorm1d → GELU → Dropout(0.30)
⟶ Linear(2048 → 1024) → BatchNorm1d → GELU → Dropout(0.30)
⟶ Linear(1024 → 2048) ⟶ Logits z in R^2048 ⟶ σ(z) = p_hat in [0, 1]^2048
Hyperparameter Optimized Value Scientific Rationale & Optimization Strategy
Input Resolution 12,001 Dimensions 12,000 uniform bins (m/z in [0, 1200] Da, Delta = 0.1 Da) + 1 normalized precursor m/z. Captures fine isotope splits.
Hidden Layer Hierarchy [2048, 1024] Funnel architecture compresses high-dimensional sparse inputs into dense latent structural embeddings.
Total Learnable Parameters 28,784,896 (28.78M) Sufficient capacity to memorize and generalize fragmentation pathways across 275,000 distinct chemical scaffolds.
Activation Function GELU Gaussian Error Linear Units smooth gradient flow and prevent dead neurons, outperforming standard ReLU on 95% zero bins.
Internal Normalization BatchNorm1d (all layers) Stabilizes covariate shift across 18,849 mini-batches per epoch, preventing gradient vanishing in early layers.
Dropout Regularization p = 0.30 Applied after each hidden layer. Forces distributed feature representations and prevents co-adaptation of weights.
Optimizer & Weight Decay AdamW (1.0 × 10^-5) Decoupled weight decay prevents L2 regularization distortion in momentum-based optimizers (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999).
Initial Learning Rate 3.0 × 10^-4 Discovered via learning rate range test; enables rapid initial descent without loss divergence.
LR Decay Schedule Cosine Annealing Decays smoothly from 3.0 × 10^-4 to 2.06 × 10^-7 across all 60 epochs, enabling deep saddle-point escaping.
Gradient Norm Clipping ||g||_2 ≤ 5.0 Guards against extreme backpropagation gradients produced by rare, massive precursor adducts.
Batch Size 128 Provides optimal stochastic gradient regularization while maintaining GPU Tensor Core compute utilization.
Training Iterations 60 Epochs (1,130,940 Steps) Executed across 52.7 hours of continuous university cluster GPU execution.
Spectral Intensity Scaling I_scaled = sqrt(I) / I_max Square-root compression boosts weak diagnostic fragment ions relative to massive base peaks.
Peak Cutoff Floor 1% Base Peak Intensity Removes electronic detector baseline noise while preserving true chemical fragmentation peaks.
Target Chemical Fingerprint ECFP4 (Morgan r=2, 2048b) Encodes circular atomic environments up to diameter 4 bonds, the gold standard for metabolomic identification.

Candidate Retrieval & Precursor Mass Filtering
Dr. Asif Assad

5. End-to-End Inference Pipeline & The ±15 ppm Mass Filter

The initial university lab codebase contained a critical retrieval bottleneck: the candidate retrieval script performed brute-force Tanimoto comparisons across all 275,810 candidates without checking whether the candidate molecule's mass physically matched the mass spectrometer precursor ion. We diagnosed and resolved this issue through physical monoisotopic mass calculations:

Physical Precursor Mass Constraint Resolution:
1. We parsed chemical formulas from the 2.54M training dataset and computed high-precision monoisotopic neutral masses for all 275,810 candidate molecules into candidate_masses.npy.
2. For each query spectrum, the theoretical neutral mass is calculated from the precursor ion m/z and the ionization adduct Delta_adduct (e.g., [M+H]+ → -1.007276 Da, [M+Na]+ → -22.989218 Da).
3. We apply a strict ±15 ppm physical tolerance window:
|MW_candidate - M_neutral| ≤ M_neutral × 15 × 10^-6
4. Result: Shrinks the search space from 275,810 candidates down to ~80 chemically plausible candidates per spectrum. The neural network's 84.1% precision then easily ranks the correct molecule into the Top 1–3 positions.

InChIKey14 Deduplication for Maximum Submission Entropy

Tandem mass spectrometry fragments molecules via collision, measuring fragment mass-to-charge ratios (m/z). It cannot distinguish stereocenters (e.g., D-glucose vs. L-glucose) or minor tautomeric forms. Full SMILES or 27-character InChIKeys encode stereochemistry.

The first 14 characters of an InChIKey (inchikey14) represent the planar molecular connectivity (molecular skeleton and atom-bond graph). When generating the Top-25 submission, we deduplicate candidate molecules by their inchikey14. This prevents wasting slots on multiple stereoisomers of the same skeleton, giving the submission 25 distinct chances to hit the true target on the Kaggle leaderboard.

Mathematical Formulations & Submission Verification
Dr. Asif Assad

7. Rigorous Mathematical Formulations & Proofs

A. CID Fragmentation Kinetics (RRKM / QET Theory)

In collision-induced dissociation, precursor molecular ions are energized by inelastic collisions with inert buffer gas (N2 or Ar). According to Rice-Ramsperger-Kassel-Marcus (RRKM) and Quasi-Equilibrium Theory (QET), the unimolecular dissociation rate constant k(E) for an energized ion with internal energy E and critical activation energy E0 is:

k(E) = [ σ · N‡(E - E0) ] / [ h · ρ(E) ]

where σ is the reaction pathway degeneracy, N‡(E - E0) is the sum of vibrational states in the transition state, h is Planck's constant, and ρ(E) is the density of states of the reactant ion. Because internal energy distributions vary across collision energies, identical molecules produce variable peak intensities. Our multi-scale neural network learns the topological invariants underlying these branching fragmentation kinetics.

B. Binary Cross-Entropy with Logits Objective Function

To train the 2048-dimensional multi-label regression stably without numerical underflow:

L(z, y*) = - (1 / 2048) ∑_{b=1}^{2048} [ y*_b · log σ(z_b) + (1 - y*_b) · log(1 - σ(z_b)) ]

C. Continuous-Binary Tanimoto Similarity Formula

Retrieval matches predicted continuous probabilities p_hat in [0, 1]^2048 against candidate binary fingerprints d_j in {0, 1}^2048:

T(p_hat, d_j) = ( d_j · p_hat ) / ( ∑ d_{jb} + ∑ p_hat_b - d_j · p_hat + ε )

D. Official Evaluation Metric: MRR@25 on InChIKey14

MRR@25 = (1 / |Q|) ∑_{q=1}^{|Q|} [ max_{1 ≤ k ≤ 25} { I( InChIKey14(C_{q, k}) == InChIKey14(M_q*) ) / k } ]
